record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: In branch-cut cosmology, how should the apparent cosmic anisotropy associated with the smoothness problem of small temperature fluctuations be explained consistently, especially in the final stage of contraction where the authors say a negative value of the dimensionless thermodynamic parameter epsilon reverses the scaling behavior of the anisotropy-related ratio while the remaining ratios stay locked in?

evidence.quote: The anisotropy associated with the smoothness problem of small temperature fluctuations has a peculiar solution that still lacks a more consistent explanation.

This is because, in the final phase of the contraction process, choosing the epsilon parameter with a negative value (dark matter?), the scaling behavior of the ratio is reversed, simultaneously assuming the remaining ratios are locked in.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cosmological model in which the spatial scale factor is replaced by a complex, branch-cut analytic continuation of the Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker scale factor, so that the universe undergoes a contracting phase followed by an expanding phase joined across a horizontal branch cut (no singular Big Bang). In an anisotropic Bianchi-type generalization of this background, introduce the dimensionless ratios that measure, in units of the total energy density, the contributions of (i) spatial curvature, (ii) matter, (iii) radiation, and (iv) shear anisotropy, as functions of a thermodynamic-like dimensionless parameter ε that characterizes the equation of state of an effective fluid driving the contraction/expansion. Assume that during the final stage of contraction the curvature, matter, and radiation ratios remain "locked in" (i.e. effectively constant in their relative scaling), while the anisotropy-related ratio scales as a power of the scale factor whose sign is governed by ε, so that taking ε<0 (interpreted as a dark-matter-like component) reverses the scaling behavior of the anisotropy ratio.

Problem. Within this framework, give a fully consistent dynamical explanation of how the smoothness (near-isotropy) of the cosmic temperature fluctuations can arise: specifically, derive conditions on ε and on the locked-in ratios under which the anisotropy ratio is driven to arbitrarily small values at the end of the contracting phase and remains small throughout the subsequent expansion, and show that such conditions are compatible with the analytic structure of the branch-cut scale factor and with the observed level of CMB temperature fluctuations.
artifact.status_search_result: Branch-cut cosmology is a recent proposal and the smoothness/anisotropy issue in its contracting phase is explicitly flagged by its proponents as lacking a consistent explanation. No follow-up work appears to have resolved this; the question seems to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: The anisotropy associated with the smoothness problem of small temperature fluctuations has a peculiar solution that still lacks a more consistent explanation.
status_evidence.claim: The authors who introduced this framework state that the anisotropy/smoothness issue in branch-cut cosmology still lacks a consistent explanation, indicating an open problem.
